newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Northeast spot power steady amid mild weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Northeast spot power steady amid mild weather.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices Friday in the northeastern U.S. held mostly steady against Thursday's levels as mild temperatures were forecast to stay into early next week.
Spring-like weather, about five to 15 degrees Fahrenheit above normal, was expected to linger in most of the Northeast, but Arctic air would make its way into northern New England over the week.

Peak, non-firm electricity prices (including transmission costs) for Monday delivery in the western part of the New York Power Pool (NYPP) were assessed at $21.00-$23.00 a megawatt hour (MWh), up from Thursday's $20.00-$21.00 range.
Off-peak, non-firm power for next-day delivery in western NYPP remained at $14.00-$15.00.
In eastern NYPP, peak, non-firm power for Monday stayed at $25.00-$26.00/MWh.
Eastern NYPP electricity for off-peak, non-firm delivery Monday were still assessed at a $18.00-$20.00 range.

In the New England Power Pool (NEPOOL), peak, non-firm electricity for Monday at Northeast Utilities' (NU) border were valued at $31.00-$34.00/MWh, flat from Thursday's quotes for day-ahead scheduling.
Non-firm, off-peak NEPOOL power for next-day delivery to the NU border was remained at $21.00-$23.00.
Swing prices of delivery to the New York City gate were valued in the high $3.40 per million British thermal unit (mmBtu) range, compared with Thursday's $3.40-$3.60.
On the New York Mercantile Exchange, February Henry Hub natgas futures closed up 21.6 cents/mmBtu at $3.106.
